paper.title: Optimizing the fluoride removal from water using a novel adsorbent prepared from Waste Cerastoderma edule shell with Kinetic, Equilibrium, and Thermodynamic studies
paper.abstract: Abstract Conversion of waste materials into useful resource is emerging and development of a low-cost adsorbent from waste materials into useful adsorbent for defluoridation of water is no exception. The present research developed a new chemical-thermal activated adsorbent from calcium carbonate rich marine waste. Cerastoderma Edule shell material for defluoridation of water. Taguchi’s L16 orthogonal array is applied to optimize the adsorption process for maximum (F-) removal from water. Analysis of mean using S/N ratios, provided optimum values of process parameters as temperature 30°C, initial (F-) concentration 20 ppm, dosage 4 g/L, pH 3, and contact time of 60 minutes for maximum removal efficiency of 94% with adsorbent capacity as 4.8 mg/g. Analysis of variance revealed the percentage contribution of parameters as Temperature 5.24%; Initial F concentration 16.78%; pH 25.49%; Dose 18.81%; and contact time 11.45%, showing pH as the most contributing parameter. For better understating of adsorption process using waste Cerastoderma Edule shell adsorbent, equilibrium, kinetics and thermodynamic studies are also conducted on optimum conditions. Equilibrium studies revealed it better fit to Freundlich isotherm signifying that the process involved multilayer adsorption on a heterogeneous surface. Best fitting kinetic model pseudo-second order and the thermodynamic analysis revealed that the process was spontaneous, endothermic, and entropy driven, favouring higher temperatures. For adsorbent material characterization, SEM and EDS tests indicate the adsorption (F-) on the adsorbent material, while FTIR test revealed that the other surface functional groups remained similar through adsorption process. The present adsorbent developed from marine waste Cerastoderma Edule shell is effective for defluoridation.

paper.title: Molecularly engineered zwitterionic‑fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte for durable Ah-level zinc-ion batteries
paper.abstract: Aqueous zinc-ion batteries are considered suitable candidates for grid storage but suffer from Zn dendrites and water-induced side reactions. Incorporating appropriate hydrophobic moieties into hydrogel electrolytes is an effective strategy to reduce water activity and widen the electrochemical stability window. To further advance this molecular design framework and enable precise interphase modulation, we report a molecularly engineered zwitterionic-fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte. Within the polymer network, the rationally introduced hydrophobic fluoroalkyl moieties (–CH2CF3) strengthen hydrogen bonds between hydrophilic units and water, thereby reducing water activity and mitigating parasitic reactions. Meanwhile, the zincophilic zwitterionic units (–SO3–, –N+(CH3)3) facilitate rapid and directional Zn2+ transport, with a Zn2+ transference number of 0.76. These tailored functional groups synergistically promote the in-situ formation of an organic–inorganic solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Zn negative electrode stability, achieving over 900 h of Zn plating/stripping at 5.0 mA cm–2 and 5.0 mAh cm–2. Furthermore, Zn | |MnO2 pouch cells incorporating this electrolyte deliver a capacity of ~1 Ah and operate for over 700 h, indicating the potential of this electrolyte for large-scale energy storage applications. Aqueous zinc-ion batteries promise safe energy storage but suffer from dendrites and side reactions. Here, authors engineer a zwitterionic fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte to suppress these issues, enabling durable, dendrite free, Ah-level pouch cells.

paper.title: A Robust Gel Polymer Electrode with Controlled-Release Polymerization towards Practical Lithium-Sulfur Batteries
paper.abstract: While rational electrode engineering has promoted the kinetics of lithium-sulfur batteries, persistent lithium polysulfide diffusion continues to undermine the cyclability of conventional liquid electrolyte systems. We propose a quasi-solid gel electrode design that integrates the sulfur species-blocking attributes of a solid-state system within a liquid electrolyte framework. This is achieved through a well-designed free radical-controlled-release polymerization strategy, which precisely governs the formation of a processable poly(ethyl cyanoacrylate) network. This approach enables secondary in situ gelation triggered by electrolyte infiltration, forming gel-phase electrode architectures. Mechanistically, the resulting gel-based electrode provides dynamically adaptive stress dissipation to accommodate volume variations, establishes continuous ion-permeable pathways for deeper positive electrode discharge, and acts as a synergistic physico-chemical barrier for sulfur species confinement. As a result, the positive electrode delivers a high initial capacity of 812.8 mA h g–1 at 2 C and sustains stable cycling operation over 1000 cycles. A 1.7 Ah-level pouch cell demonstrates potential for a sustained power supply for an unmanned aerial vehicle. A free radical-controlled-release polymerization strategy precisely governs the formation of poly(ethyl cyanoacrylate) network. Secondary gelation triggered by electrolyte infiltration leads to the effective enhancement of lithium-sulfur batteries.

paper.title: Carbon Nanodots Modulate Ciprofloxacin Adsorption onto Polylactic Acid Microplastics in Aquatic Environments: Behavior and Mechanistic Insights
paper.abstract: Abstract To investigate the influence of carbon dots (CDs) on the adsorption behavior of ciprofloxacin (CIP) by microplastics, willow leaves were used as a carbon source to synthesize CDs via a hydrothermal method, which were subsequently employed to modify polylactic acid (CDs-PLA). The materials were characterized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR). Batch adsorption experiments were conducted to evaluate the adsorption performance and underlying mechanisms of both CDs and CDs-PLA toward CIP. The adsorption process was analyzed using the pseudo-second-order kinetic model, as well as the Langmuir and Freundlich isotherm models. The results demonstrated that the synthesized CDs exhibited a uniform spherical morphology with an average particle size of 5.95 ± 0.07 nm, an ordered surface lattice, and abundant oxygen-containing functional groups including C = O, –OH, –COOH, and C–O–C. The adsorption of CIP onto both PLA and CDs-PLA followed the pseudo-second-order kinetic model and was well described by the Langmuir and Freundlich isotherm models, displaying both monolayer and multilayer adsorption characteristics, with chemisorption as the predominant mechanism.

paper.title: Reply to: Should we return to probability distributions to represent interfacial reactivity?
paper.abstract: The central argument of our Perspective 1 article is that continuum-scale models should represent interfacial properties using probability distributions of surface descriptors rather than fixed average values. Traditional methods address surface heterogeneity by treating a surface as a collection of distinct reactive site types, with each type characterized by fixed equilibrium or reaction rate constants. For instance, in surface complexation modeling (SCM), multi-parameter approach assigns constant values to different site types, effectively representing heterogeneity as an assembly of discrete site classes (see, for example Table II in ref. 2 and Eq. (5) in ref. 3 ). Similarly, other studies 4 , 5 discussed in the Comment propose that a surface may be treated as an assembly of different groups of sites, each group characterized by its own affinity constant and adsorption isotherm (see for example, Eq. (27) in ref. 4 or Table 1 in ref. 5 ). However, the probabilities in these models reflect the likelihood of occurrence of each site type, not variability in the chemical descriptors themselves.

Branched-type nanocluster-junction fluorofluidic-gels for interface-adaptive thermal conduction and mechanical resistance
paper.abstract: With the miniaturization and high integration of microelectronic devices, efficient thermal management is increasingly critical. Conventional thermal interface materials often suffer from a certain degree of mismatch between their thermal conductivity and contact thermal resistance. Herein, we develop a thermal interface fluorofluidic-gel with a branched-type nanocluster-junction network. Benefiting from the interfacial infiltration enabled by the branched-junction fluoronetwork and the efficient thermal pathways constructed by thermal conductive nanocomposites, the fluorofluidic-gel exhibits a high thermal conductivity of 5.89 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹ and a low contact thermal resistance of 0.15 cm²·K·W⁻¹. It also achieves reversible adhesion and mechanical resistance, with an adhesive strength of 189.3 kPa, adhesion energy of 220.3 J·m⁻² and impact resistance of 3.91 J·cm⁻¹. In addition, this gel maintains thermal stability from −80 °C to 300 °C and exhibits an electrical breakdown strength exceeding 24 kV/mm. We ‌anticipate‌ that adaptive thermal interface fluorofluidic-gel presents a promising solution for high-heat-flux electronic thermal management. ‘Conventional thermal interface materials often suffer from a certain degree of mismatch between their thermal conductivity and contact thermal resistance. paper.title: Substrate coupling and inhibition in human Na+-dependent Cl−/HCO3− exchanger NCBE (SLC4A10)
paper.abstract: Maintaining pH homoeostasis is essential for neuronal excitability and for regulating cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). The Na⁺-dependent Cl⁻/HCO3⁻ exchanger, NCBE (SLC4A10), abundant in the choroid plexus, contributes to CSF pH control by mediating bicarbonate flux, yet its molecular mechanism has remained unclear. Here we report cryo-EM structures of human NCBE in multiple functional states, revealing conserved binding sites for Na⁺, Cl⁻, and HCO3⁻, as well as an unexpected K⁺ site indicating relaxed cation selectivity. The inhibitor DIDS binds above the substrate cavity, locking NCBE in an outward-facing conformation and defining a subfamily-selective inhibitory mechanism. Functional assays and molecular dynamics simulations support the coordination of ions and the inhibitory effects. Comparison with an AlphaFold3-predicted inward-facing model suggests an elevator-like transport mechanism and delineates the conformational transitions in Na⁺-dependent HCO₃⁻ transporters. Together, these findings establish a structural framework for NCBE and offer insights into ion coupling and pharmacological modulation within the SLC4 family.

paper.title: Controlled motion of polar vortex boundary in oxide heterostructures
paper.abstract: Polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures hold promise for high-density, energy-efficient nanoelectronics, but their controlled motion remains elusive due to strong pinning and lattice-coupled dynamics. Here, we report real-time observation of vortex boundary motion in PbTiO₃/SrTiO₃ heterostructures using localized trailing electric fields applied via a conductive atomic force microscopy (AFM) tip. The vortex boundaries show reversible motion that depends on both field polarity and AFM tip trajectory. By precisely steering the tip along specific paths, we achieve controlled, reconfigurable vortex boundary motion with remarkable stability over extended periods. In-situ scanning transmission electron microscopy further confirmed the controlled motion of the vortex boundary. Phase-field simulations reveal that this motion is governed by switching of the zigzag pattern at the vortex core, pinpointing the underlying physical mechanism. These results establish the feasibility of externally controlled vortex boundary motion, advancing both fundamental understanding of polar topological dynamics and prospects for next-generation polar-vortex-based nanoelectronic devices. The authors demonstrate reversible electric-field control of polar vortex boundaries in PbTiO₃/SrTiO₃ heterostructures, revealing their real-time motion and providing a pathway toward reconfigurable, low-power, high density topological nanoelectronics.

paper.title: Machine learning-enabled prediction and interpretation of spectroscopic properties in Nd and Y co-doped fluorite platform via local coordination engineering
paper.abstract: The design of advanced laser materials demands precise control over the relationship between local structure and spectroscopic performance. However, conventional approaches struggle to quantitatively link complex coordination environments with spectral properties in rare-earth-doped systems, particularly for correlated 4f-electron states. Herein, we present a machine learning-enabled compositional optimization strategy for tailoring the spectral characteristics of neodymium and yttrium-co-doped fluorites, a platform featuring a wealth of structures and spectroscopic properties, via local coordination engineering. By integrating experimental spectroscopy with structural data, we train interpretable models—including Linear Regression (LR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)—to predict key spectroscopic parameters from the relative fractions of three dominant polyhedral motifs. The resultant models reveal, through Shapley value analysis, distinct roles of each structural unit in governing absorption, emission, and lifetime behavior. This data-driven framework not only overcomes limitations of traditional Density Functional Theory (DFT) in treating localized 4f states but also provides a scalable pathway for the intelligent compositional optimization of broadband, high-repetition-rate laser materials. This work highlights the effectiveness of combining local structural descriptors with interpretable machine learning to elucidate structure–property relationships in rare-earth-doped fluorite systems, providing guidance for the design of advanced laser materials.

Beyond Multiscale: A Neural-Network-Unified Molecular Model for Asymmetry-Free Dynamics Simulation
paper.abstract: Abstract Adaptive multiscale simulations, such as adaptive quantum mechanics (QM)/molecular mechanics (MM), are indispensable for investigating complex solution dynamics but historically suffer from a fundamental dilemma: the dynamic exchange of identical solvent molecules across different model resolutions introduces an energetic asymmetry under solvent exchange (specifically, a permutation asymmetry where physically identical molecules are treated indistinguishably yet subjected to different force fields depending on their instantaneous positions). This asymmetry forces a prohibitive trade-off between severe structural distortions and the violation of Hamiltonian conservation (continuous energy drift). To resolve this issue, we propose the “Integrated Molecular Model,” a paradigm-shifting framework that unifies multiple resolutions into a single, dynamically consistent potential. By employing a neural network that takes only the multiscale weight functions as input descriptors, our model learns to systematically cancel the nonphysical transition forces originating from spatial discontinuities. As a proof-of-concept, we validated this unified framework on bulk water, aqueous ionic solutions, and reactive hydronium ions. Our approach not only faithfully restores artifact-free solvation structures but also strictly conserves the Hamiltonian, enabling stable, long-term simulations under the microcanonical (NVE) ensemble. Consequently, the model successfully eliminates artificial thermostat-induced breathing modes, allowing for the rigorous evaluation of intrinsic dynamical properties such as diffusion coefficients. Furthermore, owing to its physically informed network design, the correction potential introduces less than 2% additional computational overhead and demonstrates remarkable zero-shot transferability across chemically similar ionic species. By eradicating the inherent asymmetry of adaptive multiscale modeling, this highly scalable framework establishes a robust foundation for high-fidelity simulations of complex condensed-phase phenomena, including reactive dynamics at solid–liquid interfaces and ion transport in battery electrolytes.

Microlightning: Avalanche-Driven Blue Emission and Reactive-Species Formation in Charged Microdroplets
paper.abstract: Abstract Charged microdroplets have recently been observed in experiments performed without a strong externally imposed field to emit flashes of blue light and initiate chemical reactions, a new phenomenon referred to as “microlightning.” This observation adds to a growing body of evidence that charged microdroplets can host redox chemistry not accessible in bulk solution, yet the mechanistic origin and chemical consequences of this emission remain poorly understood. A fundamental chemical question regarding spontaneous microdroplet reactivity thus naturally arises: can electrostatic energy stored on a microdroplet be converted into chemical activation, including molecular excitation, ionization, and reactive-species formation? Here, we establish a framework that links droplet charging, avalanche dynamics, and the resulting reactive-species and photon production. Under the local-field approximation, Townsend theory establishes analytical scaling for finite avalanches in isolated heavily charged droplets; particle-in-cell Monte Carlo simulations quantify multiplication up to ∼1000 and resolve electron fates via ionization, excitation, and attachment, generating reactive oxygen and hydrogen species (e.g., OH•, O2•–, and H•) or their precursors relevant to microdroplet-accelerated organic reactions and atmospheric chemistry. Further, pairs of oppositely charged droplets create intensified fields that enable detectable N2 second-positive-system emission and promote significant reactive-species formation. Finally, we identify the necessary conditions for microlightning: micrometer-scale droplets carrying substantial fractions of the Rayleigh limit, seed electrons, and ionization-enhancing gas environments, providing a predictive basis for understanding microdroplet reactivity in electrospray and other reaction platforms. These findings characterize microlightning as a form of finite-size interfacial plasma-chemistry, bridging microscopic discharges with macroscopic lightning.

paper.title: High-entropy enabled two-dimensional ferroelectricity and memristive synapses in van der Waals layered materials
Electrohydraulic Shock-Induced Plasma Pinch Dynamics and Fast Neutron Generation Using Novel Composite Refractory Electrodes
paper.abstract: Abstract Building directly upon our foundational demonstration of extreme high-pressure high-temperature (HPHT) synthesis of nanostructured tungsten-carbide/lithium-6 hydride (WC–Co/ 6 LiH) composites, this study delivers an extended experimental investigation into high-energy plasma pinch dynamics, electrode microstructural durability, and transient nuclear reaction kinetics during severe electrohydraulic shock (EHS) discharges in heavy water (D 2 O). Industrial precursor matrices (VK-6 and VK-8) consolidated under hydrostatic pressures of P = 7.6 GPa were precision-machined into composite electrodes and evaluated under sub-microsecond high-voltage breakdown. Multiphysics experimental plasma diagnostics combined with time-resolved soft X-ray continuum slope analysis confirmed a peak core electron temperature k B T e = 3.02 ± 0.25 keV ( T e ≈ 3.5 × 10 7 K) and dynamic pinch-induced shock pressures exceeding 100 GPa (> 1 Mbar). High-resolution time-of-flight (TOF) fast-neutron spectrometry revealed a prominent, thermally broadened high-energy neutron emission peak centered near ~ 14.1 MeV ( E n = 14.1 ± 0.4 MeV ) with a characteristic yield of ~ (1.2 ± 0.15) × 10 5 neutrons/pulse, matched by post-shot quadrupole mass-spectrometric detection of 4 He and 3 He gaseous ash. To address fundamental questions regarding isotopic carrier behavior, parallel experiments were conducted using composite electrodes containing pure metallic 6 Li instead of the hydride carrier ( 6 LiH). Comparative evaluation demonstrated that both configurations yield equivalent nuclear and thermal signatures within diagnostic resolution. Given the extreme transient environment of the EHS breakdown, pulse-to-pulse hydrodynamic variations exceeded any consistently resolvable difference attributable specifically to the hydride phase. A comprehensive Saha–Boltzmann continuum-lowering ionization balance model and Mie–Grüneisen equation-of-state analysis are formulated to describe the compressed discharge channel.

paper.title: Enhanced Orbital Hall Effect via sp,d-Coupling-Engineered Orbital Texture
paper.abstract: Abstract The discovery of the orbital Hall effect (OHE) has established the orbital degree of freedom as a critical enabler for energy-efficient magnetic memory technologies. While massive materials have demonstrated the ability to produce giant OHE based on their unique orbital texture, a general method for realizing giant OHE in a CMOS-compatible material remains elusive. Here, we propose heavy-element doping of Cu base as a general strategy to boost OHE via sp,d -coupling-engineered orbital texture. We synthesize two sample series with Ni and CoFeB ferromagnetic layers on doped Cu base, i.e. , Cu 7 X 1 alloys (X = Ta, W, Tb, Mn) to separate OHE and spin Hall effect (SHE) contributions. Spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance measurements demonstrate that OHE-induced spin-orbital torque efficiency is enhanced approximately sixfold in Cu 7 X 1 alloys, comparable to heavy metal of Ta and W. Current-induced magnetization switching experiments confirm this enhancement, with a significant reduction in critical switching current density. Theoretical calculations reveal that the enhanced OHE originates from orbital coupling between Cu 4 s /4 p orbitals near the Fermi level and 5 d orbitals of dopant element with large orbital angular momentum. This work provides a general strategy to realize significant OHE in CMOS-compatible materials, enabling high-efficiency orbitronic applications.

paper.title: Defect-Driven Engineering of Nitrogen-Doped Reduced Graphene Oxide Membranes for Dye Separation
paper.abstract: Abstract In this work, a controlled hydrothermal method is employed for the simultaneous reduction of graphene oxide (GO) and incorporation of nitrogen heteroatoms into and over the GO surface. Three concentrations (N-1, N-3, N-5) are synthesised to track the doping-dependent structural evolution from amorphous GO to nanocrystalline nitrogen-doped reduced graphene oxide (N-rGO). XRD analysis confirms the complete disappearance of the GO (001-0.89 nm) peak and the emergence of a broadened graphitic (002-0.33 nm) reflection, with N-5 exhibiting enhanced crystallinity.XPS deconvolution validates the formation of C–N bonds and nitrogen incorporation with a substantial rise in C = C content for N-5, indicating improved π-conjugation/graphitic domain. HRTEM micrographs and SAED patterns show the transition from a disordered GO lattice in N-1 to well-defined diffraction spots and reduced interlayer spacing from (0.36 → 0.33 nm) in N-5, confirming the development of few-layer crystalline N-rGO sheets. The membranes exhibit ultrahigh rejection efficiencies (> 98.8%) for methylene blue, methyl orange, and rhodamine B, along with high permeance (up to ~ 126 L m⁻² h⁻¹ bar⁻¹) under low operating pressures (2–4 bar). Overall, this study establishes a scalable route for tailoring defect chemistry and crystallinity in N-rGO, demonstrating its strong potential for advanced water purification, catalytic, and optoelectronic applications.

paper.title: Out-of-Distribution Inverse Design of Elastic Networks with Differentiable Graph Neural Network Molecular Dynamics
paper.abstract: Abstract Machine-learning-based inverse design can accelerate the discovery of materials with targeted properties, but conventional structure--property models often require large training datasets and generalize poorly beyond their training distribution. Here, we present a differentiable inverse design framework based on a graph neural network molecular dynamics simulator. By combining a short dynamical initialization with physics-based refinement during simulation, the framework enables optimization well beyond the conditions represented in the training data. Using disordered elastic networks, we show that a simulator trained only on non-auxetic systems with Poisson's ratios between 0.1 and 0.4 can design strongly auxetic networks with values as low as -0.3. The framework also produces stress--strain responses outside the range observed during training, creates localized mechanical defects absent from the training data, and generalizes across system size, enabling optimization of networks tested up to 5000 nodes despite being trained only on networks with fewer than 200 nodes.
paper.tldr: 该框架通过将短时动力学初始化与物理修正相结合，在超出训练分布的弹性网络逆向设计中实现了显著优化的性能。

paper.title: Effect of γ-Irradiation on the Electrical and Photoelectric Properties of Cu-Intercalated Gase Single Crystals
paper.abstract: Abstract The effects of γ-irradiation on the electrical and photoelectric properties of Cu-intercalated layered GaSe single crystals were systematically investigated. Cu intercalation was performed electrochemically for different durations, and the samples intercalated for 60 min, which exhibited the highest electrical conductivity, were selected for subsequent investigations. The electrical properties of Cu-intercalated GaSe single crystals were studied at absorbed γ-irradiation doses of 0, 1, 5, 10, and 15 kGy. Analysis of the temperature-dependent electrical conductivity revealed that the activation energy increased from 0.04 to 0.07 eV in the low-temperature region (100–250 K) and from 0.18 to 0.30 eV in the high-temperature region (250–300 K) with increasing irradiation dose. At the same time, the room-temperature electrical conductivity exhibited a non-monotonic dose dependence, increasing at 1 kGy and subsequently decreasing at higher doses. The spectral photocurrent was measured at 300 and 110 K under a constant bias voltage of 50 V. A decrease in photocurrent was observed after Cu intercalation and at 1 kGy, whereas a pronounced increase occurred at 15 kGy, reaching maximum values of 5.93⋅10 − 6 A at 300 K and 3.20⋅10 − 6 A at 110 K. These results demonstrate that Cu intercalation and γ-irradiation modify charge transport and photoelectric response in GaSe single crystals in a manner dependent on intercalation time, irradiation dose, and temperature.
paper.tldr: γ射线照射会改变铜插层GaSe单晶的激活能，但摘要未提供电学和光电性能变化的完整数值证据。

paper.title: From Explainable Machine Learning to Physics-Guided Design Rules for Inorganic Phosphors
paper.abstract: Abstract The rational design of inorganic phosphors with targeted emission wavelengths is challenging because luminescence depends on strongly coupled structural, electronic, and excitation-dependent factors. Machine-learning studies in this area often prioritize predictive accuracy without systematically evaluating descriptor reproducibility and physical interpretability. Here, we develop a physics-guided explainable machine-learning framework that combines multi-method feature selection, descriptor stability analysis, and physicochemical interpretation for emission-wavelength prediction. A curated dataset of 2327 single-dopant phosphor compositions, initially represented by 125 physicochemical descriptors, was refined to 46 physically meaningful descriptors. Twelve complementary feature-selection methods were evaluated using eight stability metrics and 10-fold cross-validation. Pearson correlation and ANOVA-F, which are mathematically related univariate criteria for measuring linear association, identified the same seven-descriptor subset with complete 10/10 fold-level reproducibility. The resulting Random Forest model achieved a mean cross-validated R 2 = 0.9308, MAE = 7.78 nm, and RMSE = 22.55 nm. The seven-descriptor model retained essentially the same predictive performance as the best fully reproducible 24-descriptor model while reducing descriptor dimensionality by about 71% relative to that model and by about 86% relative to the full physically meaningful candidate space. Under 10-fold cross-validation, RF and GB achieved R 2 values of 0.9192 and 0.9023, respectively. SHAP analysis, descriptor ablation, interaction analysis, and complementary feature-importance methods consistently identified the same descriptor hierarchy. The ionic radius of the emission-center site was the dominant predictor, followed by excitation source and dopant valency. These results suggest four practical considerations for phosphor screening, namely activator-site compatibility, dopant oxidation state, host chemical environment, and excitation conditions. The results show that descriptor selection should consider not only predictive accuracy but also reproducibility, compactness, robustness, and physical interpretability.
paper.tldr: 该研究提出的物理引导可解释机器学习框架在2327个单掺杂荧光粉数据集中，通过多方法特征选择和描述符稳定性分析，实现了发射波长预测并揭示了关键物理设计规则。

paper.title: Ultrasonic Acoustic Cavitation Driven Hydrogen Degassing in Molten Aluminium Alloys and Its Effects on Porosity and Mechanical Properties
paper.abstract: Abstract High-intensity ultrasonic treatment of molten aluminium alloys generates acoustic cavitation — transient formation and collapse of micro-bubbles in the melt — which provides a powerful physical mechanism for dissolved hydrogen removal without the use of halogen or toxic process gases. This study presents a systematic investigation of the ultrasonic molten metal treatment system applied to AA-series aluminium alloys during continuous strip casting. Experiments were conducted at melt temperatures from 680°C to 760°C with ultrasonic frequencies of 19–21 kHz and varying power densities. The density index (DI) was measured before and after treatment using the reduced pressure test (RPT). Metallographic analysis of transverse cross-sections of cast foil and billet samples was performed to characterise porosity distribution, pore morphology, and grain size. Vickers hardness measurements were taken at multiple positions across the cross-section. Results demonstrate that ultrasonic treatment achieves a density index below 0.08 cc/100g — below the threshold required for defect-free 6-micron aluminium foil production — compared to greater than 0.15 cc/100g observed without treatment. Porosity elimination and grain refinement via the Hall-Petch mechanism are attributed to cavitation-induced degassing and acoustic streaming effects. Hardness uniformity across the cross-section improved by 22% compared to rotary degassing controls. The system eliminates the use of hex chloride and hexafluoride process gases, which are 24,000 times more damaging than CO₂ as greenhouse agents. Industrial validation was performed with nil pinholes and holes observed in 6-micron foil output and confirmed by two industrial institutions.

paper.title: Valorization of Vaccinium corymbosum Leaf Waste for Silver Nanoparticles: Characterization and In Vitro Biological Dynamics
paper.abstract: Abstract This study explores the sustainable valorization of Vaccinium corymbosum L. (blueberry) leaf waste as a potent bio-reductant and stabilizing agent for the phyto-mediated synthesis of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs). The phytochemical profiling of the leaf extract confirmed a terpene- and phenolic-rich composition, facilitating the biogenic reduction of Ag + ions. Successful formation of AgNPs was validated by UV–Vis spectroscopy, exhibiting a characteristic surface plasmon resonance (SPR) peak at 420–430 nm. Electron microscopy (SEM and TEM) revealed predominantly spherical nanostructures with a narrow size distribution (10–35 nm), while XRD analysis confirmed a high-purity face-centered cubic (FCC) crystalline lattice. FT-IR spectra highlighted the pivotal role of hydroxyl, carbonyl, and C–O functional groups in the capping and stabilization process. The synthesized AgNPs exhibited significant broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, with enhanced efficacy against Gram-positive pathogens. Mechanistic evaluations via growth kinetics demonstrated that the antibacterial action is driven by membrane disruption, intracellular leakage, and oxidative stress. Furthermore, the NPs displayed dose-dependent antibiofilm activity, complemented by the intrinsic antioxidant capacity of the leaf extract. These findings demonstrate that V. corymbosum leaf waste can be effectively transformed into high-value biofunctional nanomaterials. This eco-friendly and low-energy synthesis route aligns with circular economy principles and provides a promising platform for sustainable applications in food safety and nanobiotechnology.

paper.title: Effect of Polydispersity on the Morphological Symmetry of Poly(methyl methacrylate)-block-polystyrene Copolymer Films
paper.abstract: Abstract The effect of polydispersity of the poly(methyl methacrylate) block on the morphological symmetry of the films of diblock copolymers synthesized by two-stage reversible addition-fragmentation chain transfer polymerization of methyl methacrylate and styrene was investigated. Increasing polydispersity from 1.11 to 1.53 of PMMA includes a transition from lamellar symmetry with a periodicity of 67 nm to cubic symmetry of spherical domains (58 nm), via a mixed lamellar-spherical symmetry.

paper.title: Fabrication of Pinus pinaster’s Tannin-Engineered Silver Nanophotocatalyst for Degradation of Methylene Blue Dye
paper.abstract: Abstract The increasing demand for sustainable nanomaterials has driven the development of green synthesis strategies that replace conventional toxic reagents with renewable bioresources. Plant-derived phytochemicals provide an eco-friendly pathway for fabricating functional nanoparticles for environmental applications. Therefore, in this study, silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) were synthesized via a green approach using tannins extracted from Pinus pinaster as natural reducing and stabilizing agents, thereby eliminating the need for hazardous chemicals. The formation of Pinus pinaster’s tannin mediated AgNPs (PPT-AgNPs) was confirmed through UV–visible spectroscopy, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM–EDX), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The microscopy studies revealed that AgNPs particle sizes ranged from 15.9 to 96.4 nm. The photocatalytic activity of the synthesized AgNPs was evaluated for the degradation of methylene blue dye under UV irradiation. The photocatalytic reaction deviates from classical Arrhenius kinetics but may be governed by a balance between molecular kinetics, adsorption/desorption equilibrium and/or charge carrier recombination rates. Optimum conditions were achieved at pH 5 and 30°C, reaching a degradation efficiency of 87.37% within 5 h. Kinetic analysis showed that the degradation followed pseudo-first-order kinetics with a rate constant of 0.4961 h⁻¹. Overall, the utilization of Pinus pinaster tannins as natural reducing and stabilizing agents provides a sustainable route for AgNP fabrication, yielding photocatalysts with promising activity for wastewater treatment applications.

paper.title: Immobilized PMA on a pyridine-based rigid polymer as a heterogeneous catalyst for the synthesis of 5-aminopyrazole-4-carbonitrile
paper.abstract: Abstract Phosphomolybdic acid (PMA), characterized by strong Brønsted acidity, redox activity, and thermal stability, is a leading candidate in heterogeneous catalyst design. However, challenges such as leaching and activity loss across multiple cycles limit its practical applications. In this study, immobilizing PMA on a rigid pyridine-based polymeric framework enhances the stability of acidic sites and enables catalyst recyclability. The polymeric support, with appropriate surface area and well-defined porosity, facilitates substrate access to the active PMA sites, thereby improving catalytic efficiency. The resulting catalyst afforded high yields (65–95%) in the synthesis of 5-aminopyrazole-4-carbonitrile in short reaction times (10–90 min). Moreover, the catalyst maintained its activity over at least five consecutive cycles without significant loss. These findings indicate that integrating PMA with rigid polymeric frameworks offers a promising approach to developing heterogeneous catalysts that exhibit high efficiency, structural robustness, and recyclability with considerable potential for acid-catalyzed organic transformations.
paper.tldr: 该研究通过将磷钼酸固定在刚性吡啶基聚合物骨架上，增强了酸性位点的稳定性并实现了催化剂的可回收性，同时提升了催化效率。

paper.title: A Common Small-Molecule Inhibitor Targeting Multiple Siglecs Associated with Immune Checkpoint Suppression of Cytotoxicity and Phagocytosis
paper.abstract: Abstract Immune checkpoints are key regulators of the immune system that cancer cells exploit to evade immune surveillance. While these pathways have been targeted with antibody therapies such as PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors, other inhibitory receptors, like sialic acid-binding immunoglobulin-type lectins (Siglecs), remain clinically underexplored. Among the many Siglecs on immune cells that interact with sialosides on cancer cells, Siglec-9 and Siglec-10 are prominently expressed on macrophages within the tumor microenvironment, functioning as key inhibitory immune checkpoints that suppress macrophage-mediated phagocytosis and cytotoxicity. Similarly, Siglec-7 and Siglec-9 are expressed on NK cells, acting as primary immune checkpoints that inhibit cellular cytotoxicity. Since all Siglecs recognize sialic acids, we sought to identify a common small-molecule inhibitor to target these receptors for immunotherapy. We first chemoenzymatically synthesized more than 60 glycans, including multiantennary glycans with terminal sialic acids, and assembled them onto a glycan microarray to screen for high-affinity binders to these Siglecs. We identified several strong binders in these array assays; among them, a truncated glycolyl sialoside (R3) was found to strongly inhibit the interaction of Siglec-10 with HER2-low MCF-7 cells, substantially enhancing macrophage-mediated phagocytosis and cytotoxicity. Notably, R3 also interacts significantly with other inhibitory immune checkpoint receptors, including Siglec-5, -7, -9, -11, and -15, thereby relieving Siglec-mediated suppression and enhancing NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in cell-based assays. Structural studies are underway to investigate the binding mode of R3 with these Siglecs to guide further optimization toward a common small-molecule inhibitor targeting multiple inhibitory glyco-immune checkpoints for cancer immunotherapy.

paper.title: Cooperation of PtO 2 and Adjacent Pt 1 on In 2 O 3 Photocatalysts for Unity‐Selective Propane Dehydrogenation
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Solar‐driven direct propane dehydrogenation (PDH) represents a promising strategy to overcome the high‐temperature demands and selectivity limitations of conventional thermocatalysis, yet the identification of effective photoactive phases remains challenging. Herein, we demonstrate that photoactivated PtO 2 enables regenerable and highly selective PDH over a PtO 2 /Pt 1 ‐In 2 O 3 catalyst under mild conditions. Under simulated sunlight without external heating, the catalyst achieves a propylene formation rate of 1322.35 µmol g −1 h −1 with unity selectivity, while remaining inactive under comparable thermocatalytic conditions. In situ spectroscopic analyses combined with density functional theory calculations reveal a photoactivated dual‐site mechanism, in which PtO 2 nanoparticles function as oxidation centers for hole‐driven C─H bond activation, whereas neighboring interfacial Pt single atoms act as electron‐accepting sites to promote H 2 evolution, enabling efficient spatial separation and utilization of photogenerated charge carriers. Catalyst deactivation arises from partial reduction of PtO 2 , which can be exactly regenerated via a facile oxidative annealing process in air, affording excellent reusability. These findings identify photoactivated PtO 2 as a distinct active phase for selective PDH and provide a design principle for solar‐driven alkane valorization.

paper.title: Local characterization of global tensor network eigenstates
An Ultrathin Embedded SnO2 Interface for Water Dissociation in Bipolar Membranes and pseudo-PEM Electrolyzers
paper.abstract: Water dissociation (WD) at bipolar membrane (BPM) junctions is a key reaction in a number of electrochemical energy conversion and separation technologies. While metal oxide catalysts like SnO 2 accelerate WD, conventional particle-based deposition methods typically yield thick and morphologically heterogeneous junction layers. We report a simple aqueous precursor-treatment route that reconstructs the near-surface region of Nafion into an ultrathin SnO 2 -bearing interface. In contrast to conventional spin-coated SnO 2 , which forms a discrete particulate overlayer, the embedded interface is smooth, spatially confined, and closely integrated with the membrane. Despite this major structural difference, BPMs fabricated from SnO 2 -eb-Nafion exhibit WD performance comparable to benchmark spin-coated SnO 2 junctions. When normalized by SnO 2 loading, the embedded junction delivers a ~21-fold higher current density in an electrolyzer test cell at a total cell voltage of 2 V, highlighting improved catalyst utilization. Structural and electrochemical controls show that the high activity arises from interfacially localized SnO 2 rather than bulk SnO 2 incorporation or altered proton conductivity. The embedded route improves precursor efficiency, increases membrane junction adhesion force by 7×, and maintains stable operation under continuous elec-trolyzer testing. A preliminary pseudo-PEM water-electrolysis demonstration further shows that the embedded SnO 2 interface remains beneficial in an AEI–PEM heterojunction architecture coupled to a PGM-free Co 3 O 4 anode. These results establish precursor-based interfacial self-reconstruction as a practical route to thin, active, and mechanically integrated catalyst–membrane junctions. Keywords: Bipolar membranes; Water dissociation; Tin oxide (SnO 2 ); Ionomer interfaces; Water electrolysis

paper.title: E2Former-V3: Atom-Role-Aware Equivariant Interatomic Potentials
paper.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials enable high-level accuracy for large-scale biological simulation, yet remain costly. In aqueous systems, hydrogens and the water solvent dominate the atom count, while uniform equivariant architectures give every atom the same representation capacity and spend most of their computation on them. We introduce E2Former-V3, an atom-role-aware equivariant potential architecture that represents every atom explicitly and keeps forces conservative. A static chemical role, assigned before the backbone runs, sets each atom’s latent width and how often it is updated. Two configurations follow. E2Former-V3-Standard routes hydrogens through half as many full-width block updates, reaching a force MAE of 8.146 meV/ ˚A, slightly better than E2Former-V2 (Huang et al., 2026), at 1.75–1.84× its throughput. E2Former-V3-Flash routes hydrogens and water oxygens through a narrow stream with fewer updates, trading 3.126 meV/ ˚A higher force error for 4.00–5.85× the throughput. We run molecular dynamics over water, a salt solution and a solvated protein for 20 ps, across three ensembles and three seeds. The runs hold their target temperature, keep chemical structure intact, and reproduce the measured liquid structure to within a few hundredths of an ˚Angstrom. On the solvated protein, both production checkpoints complete the full 1 ns without water fusion, nonbonded clashes or solute collapse.

E2Former-V3-Flash routes hydrogens and water oxygens through a narrow stream with fewer updates, trading 3.126 meV/ ˚A higher force error for 4.00–5.85× the throughput. We run molecular dynamics over water, a salt solution and a solvated protein for 20 ps, across three ensembles and three seeds. The runs hold their target temperature, keep chemical structure intact, and reproduce the measured liquid structure to within a few hundredths of an ˚Angstrom. paper.title: The Chameleon Role of Interfacial Hydroxyls: Reaction-Condition-Dependent Dynamics in Methanol Electro-Oxidation
paper.abstract: Abstract The electrocatalytic oxidation of methanol on platinum represents a model system for alcohol fuel-cell chemistry, yet the precise role of interfacial hydroxyl (OH*), a key oxidative species, remains contentious and is often viewed simplistically as either a co-reactant or a poison. Herein, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations with explicit solvation were employed to transcend this binary perspective, revealing OH* as a dynamic interfacial mediator whose coverage influences methanol activation and mechanistic pathways. Under oxidative potentials, increasing OH* coverage leads to the formation of an interfacial adsorbate layer interconnected by hydrogen bonds. Frequent proton transfer within this layer facilitates spontaneous O–H bond cleavage of methanol, while fluctuations in the hydrogen-bond network further promote its pre-oxidation and activation. In contrast, OH*-mediated C–H oxidation involves a high free-energy barrier, and increasing OH* coverage reduces the availability of Pt sites required for C–H dissociation, potentially contributing to surface poisoning. Importantly, site competition induced by high OH* coverage also alters the configuration of the reaction-generated HCHO intermediate, reducing the accessibility of further C–H cleavage toward CO* while enabling direct reaction with OH* toward formate through a CO*-free pathway. Together, these results reveal a coverage-dependent trade-off among O–H activation, the availability of Pt sites for C–H bond cleavage, and subsequent pathway selection. Regulating interfacial OH* coverage therefore provides a possible means to tune methanol oxidation activity and pathway selectivity.

paper.title: Asymmetric Electrical Double Layer Charging in Ionomers under Pure Water
paper.abstract: Electrode interfaces with ionic polymers (ionomers) create local microenvironments in membrane electrolysis and other applications, yet the formation and dynamics of electrical double layers (EDLs) at ionomer|electrode interfaces are incompletely understood. Unlike traditional aqueous electrolytes with both mobile cations and anions, ionomer interfaces couple mobile counterion motion to the slower response of tethered polymer-backbone ionic groups. Studying these solid|ionomer interfaces, with pure water feed as in many technology applications, is more difficult than with conventional electrolytes due to the lack of a liquid supporting electrolyte for simple integration of counter and reference electrodes. Here, we use a membrane-electrode-assembly-inspired architecture with a lateral ionomer strip and a salt-bridged reference electrode to independently track anodic and cathodic potentials while sweeping the voltage between the two Pt-solid|ionomer interfaces in pure water. We quantify electrode-resolved non-faradaic charging and show that fixed polymer charges and mobile counterions contribute differently to interfacial capacitance. In anion-exchange ionomers, mobile Cl- responds rapidly, whereas fixed quaternary ammonium groups relax more slowly, producing a capacitance asymmetry. This asymmetry weakens when sufficient time is allowed for relaxation and is suppressed by supporting electrolyte. When Nafion cation-exchange ionomer is used instead, the results show a reversal in the sign of the asymmetry. Supporting molecular dynamics simulations establish coupled counterion motion and tethered-charge relaxation as governing features of pure-water ionomer EDLs. The work thus provides a framework for studying and ultimately designing ionomer microenvironments for membrane electrolysis and other applications. The Bigger Picture Pure-water-fed membrane electrolyzers rely on ionomers to carry charge to catalyst surfaces. Unlike soluble liquid electrolytes, ionomers contain mobile counterions and oppositely charged groups fixed to a polymer chain. The details of how these charges form electrical double layers under positive and negative polarization are not fully understood. We developed a model cell with a solid ionomer electrolyte that senses each electrode potential separately during cell operation. The measurements show asymmetric, time-dependent charging in pure water, with mobile counterions responding more rapidly than polymer-bound charge. Added electrolytes suppress this charging-rate imbalance; reversing the ionomer charge sign also reverses the asymmetry of the charging response, and a custom-synthesized more-flexible polymer backbone reduces the rate dependence of the apparent capacitance. The work here shows how the ionomer is an active part of the electrochemical interface, in addition to an ion conductor in the bulk. The platform and fundamental principles developed here are relevant to water electrolyzers, fuel cells, and other membrane-based electrochemical devices.

paper.title: Systematic fine-tuning of MACE interatomic potentials for catalysis
paper.abstract: Abstract Once trained, machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) offer a fast and accurate way to investigate catalytic reaction pathways, but their performance depends strongly on training-set design. We compared nine MLIPs developed using from-scratch (FS) training and fine-tuning (FT) of foundation models. The models were evaluated on reaction energies ( E r ) and activation barriers ( E a ) for 141 reactions, including CO 2 RR to C 2 /C 3 products, propane dehydrogenation, hydrogen intercalation on Pd, and out-of-distribution OER on metal oxides. The FS models containing 5–10% perturbed, high-energy configurations from molecular dynamics or contour exploration reduced errors by more than twofold relative to models trained only on relaxation trajectories. However, FT models were less sensitive to sampling and generalized better to out-of-distribution chemistry. For example, the FT model fine-tuned on metallic catalysts achieved an MAE of 0.30 eV for OER on iridium oxide polymorphs, while the FT model fine-tuned on metal-oxides gave an E a of 0.19 eV for CO 2 RR on Cu. The best model, fine-tuned on 49,860 configurations, performed consistently across metallic and oxide catalysts and screened 90,781 bimetallic alloys with a reaction-energy MAE of 0.15 eV, including unseen high-index surfaces. These results identify the necessary training set configurations for training transferable catalytic MLIPs.

paper.title: BranchIP: Learning Adaptive Equivariant Computation for Interatomic Potentials
paper.abstract: Equivariant machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have revolutionized atomistic modeling, but accurate treatment of complex materials and molecular systems demands expensive models. This limits simulation length- and time-scales, with tensor products a key computational bottleneck. The recent emergence of foundation-scale MLIPs further exacerbates this challenge. We present Branch Interatomic Potential (BranchIP), a single-model framework for learned adaptive tensor product computation, trained with a novel distillation loss. In our experiments on two systems of physical interest, a heterogeneous catalysis system and a proton-conducting solid acid electrolyte, BranchIP accelerates MLIPs across model sizes by up to $2.4\times$ while reducing memory usage by up to $2.6\times$. This is achieved while maintaining physical fidelity. Furthermore, the learned adaptive computation provides model interpretability by revealing which interactions demand deeper computation and showing how computational depth relates to chemical complexity and dynamics.

paper.title: Mitigating Surface Poisoning by Bidirectional Regulation for Efficient C1‐C2 Molecule Electrooxidation
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT The rational design of Pt‐based electrocatalysts to alleviate CO intermediates poisoning during electrooxidation of C1‐C2 fuels (methanol, ethanol, formic acid) presents a grand challenge. Current detoxification strategies predominantly focus on enhancing OH* formation to accelerate CO* oxidation. However, the periodic voltage/current oscillations induced by accumulated OH species are often overlooked. Such accumulation of secondary poisoning intermediates inevitably leads to a high overpotential and poor operational stability. Herein, guided by machine learning screening, we resolve this dilemma by designing ultrathin PtPdGaRuFeMo high‐entropy alloy nanosheets featuring Ga and Ru dual‐promoter sites for the bidirectional regulation of CO* and OH* adsorption. Both theoretical analysis and experimental results demonstrate that the synergistic Ga and Ru sites modulate the electronic structure of active centers, balancing the dynamic adsorption of CO* and OH* to mitigate surface poisoning. Consequently, the as‐prepared catalysts deliver excellent specific activities of 5.4 mA cm −2 for methanol and 3.5 mA cm −2 for formic acid electrooxidation, surpassing commercial Pt/C by factors of 9.7 and 12.8, respectively. This study establishes a dual‐promoter bidirectional regulation, providing a promising route offering a robust solution to the stability‐activity trade‐off in fuel‐cell electrocatalysts.

paper.title: Enhanced Hydrogen Evolution Activity of MoS 2 Through Solid Solution Modification of Its Edge Sites With Ruthenium
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT In hydrogen production, electrocatalysts featuring edge sites as active centers, modulation of its edge site coordination environment could greatly improve the reaction kinetics by effectively reducing the energy barrier. Here, we report a novel catalyst formulation obtained by the electrochemical deposition of ruthenium onto the edge sites and near‐edge basal plane of MoS 2 to yield Ru‐coordinated solid solution species. The Ru atom acts as a site for water dissociation, increasing the proton supply rate and, in turn, the catalytic activity of MoS 2 . Based on the Tafel slope, in situ Raman, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) analysis, the edge solid solution creates a locally acidic chemical environment, enhancing the kinetics of the hydrogen evolution reaction by altering the reaction pathway from Volmer–Heyrovsky observed for pristine MoS 2 to Volmer–Tafel. Edge‐coordinated Ru solid solution catalyst features a very high current density in anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) and demonstrates excellent long‐term stability when compared with other reported MoS 2 ‐ and Ru‐based catalysts. Overall, our studies demonstrate that modification of MoS 2 by the incorporation of an edge solid solution can markedly improve its catalytic activity and, therefore, represents a promising strategy for materials design in the field of renewable fuel generation.

paper.title: Electrochemical Hydroformylation with a Homogeneous Rhodium Catalyst
paper.abstract: Abstract Electrochemical hydroformylation is an attractive pathway to synthesize aldehydes at ambient conditions using electrons sourced from renewable energy as a reductant instead of hydrogen gas sourced from energy-intensive steam methane reforming. However, previously reported electrochemical hydroformylation systems have shown limited rates and selectivities using heterogeneous catalysts, motivating continued development. In this work, we report a homogeneously catalyzed system that achieved a maximum partial current density of 1.1 ± 0.1 mA cm–2 and a Faradaic efficiency of 29 ± 1% toward the conversion of styrene to 2-phenylpropanal at 5 bar CO and 25 °C. Infrared and UV-visible spectroscopies suggested that the initial Rh2Cl2(CO)4 precatalyst undergoes pressure-dependent speciation to Rh(I)–CO species in the presence of CO. Kinetic experiments revealed a complex mechanism in which the rate-determining step likely shifts between electron transfer, substrate coordination, and Rh–H bond cleavage in different substrate concentration and overpotential regimes. Looking forward, the insight from this work informs future strategies to improve the rate and selectivity of electrochemical hydroformylation and other electrochemical C–C bond formation reactions.

paper.title: Aerobic Dehydrogenation by Coupled Electrochemical Reactions Governs Room-Temperature Proton Defect Chemistry in Functional Oxides
paper.abstract: Abstract Tuning functional oxides by controlling ionic point defects is a well-established paradigm for designing tailored functionalities. At elevated temperatures, this is usually achieved by tuning ambient oxygen partial pressure (pO2) to regulate oxygen chemical potential and defect (e.g., protons and oxygen vacancies) concentrations. At room temperature, however, atmosphere-driven tuning is considered unfeasible due to sluggish surface kinetics and negligible ionic mobility. Here, using hydrogenated NdNiO3 as a model system, we show that ambient pO2 can in fact regulate hydrogen chemical potential and protonic defects through aerobic dehydrogenation driven by coupled anodic proton extraction and cathodic oxygen reduction in aqueous solutions. Using mixed-potential theory together with operando electrochemical, optical, and structural characterizations, we quantitatively analyze these coupled half-reactions and determine how pO2 modulates dehydrogenation kinetics. These insights deepen the understanding of room-temperature defect chemistry and provide guidance for designing functional oxide devices based on controlled modulation of ionic defects.

paper.title: Heterogenization of Ru(bda) Molecular Catalyst with Redox-Active and Proton-Buffering Porphyrin Linkers for Acidic Water Oxidation
paper.abstract: Abstract We report a porphyrin-bridged Ru(bda) coordination polymer integrated with carbon nanotubes, constructed from the well-defined homogeneous water oxidation catalyst in acid. The porphyrin linker simultaneously provides redox activity and proton-buffering functionality, enabling acidic water oxidation at an ultralow Ru loading (0.021 mgRu·cm–2). The resulting composite reaches current densities up to 200 mA·cm–2 in acid, exceeding previously reported molecular water oxidation catalyst-based anodes by one to two orders of magnitude. At identical metal loadings, it also outperforms both RuO2 and IrO2 benchmarks in both activity and stability. Electrochemical, spectroscopic, and theoretical results support porphyrin protonation and reversible oxidation, suggesting that ligand redox activity, together with proton management, contributes to the enhanced catalytic performance. These findings underscore the transformative potential of ligand engineering in molecular integration strategies for advancing artificial photosynthetic energy conversion systems.

paper.title: Computational Insights into Catalytic Hydrogenation over M6O8-Node MOFs: From Active-Site Engineering to Data-Driven Catalyst Design
paper.abstract: Abstract Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) containing M6O8 secondary building units (SBUs) have attracted considerable attention as hydrogenation catalysts because of their structural robustness, tunable coordination environments, and diverse opportunities for active-site engineering. In recent years, density functional theory (DFT) and related computational approaches have become indispensable tools for elucidating catalytic mechanisms and guiding catalyst design. This review summarizes recent theoretical advances in catalytic hydrogenation over M6O8-node MOFs, with particular emphasis on active-site engineering strategies, including metal doping, single-atom anchoring, metal cluster encapsulation, and ligand functionalization. Their effects on key catalytic processes, such as H2 activation, intermediate stabilization, and reaction energy barriers, are systematically discussed. We further highlight the electronic structure origins of catalytic performance, focusing on descriptors such as charge transfer, d-band center modulation, and frontier orbital interactions that govern activity and selectivity. In addition, emerging data-driven approaches are reviewed for their potential to establish structure–property relationships, enable high-throughput screening, and accelerate catalyst discovery. Current challenges in theoretical studies, including model idealization and the limited description of realistic reaction environments, are also discussed.

paper.title: NoRRA: Nonlocal Representation and Response Augmentation for Machine Learning Interatomic Models
paper.abstract: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) achieve efficient atomistic simulation by constructing each atomic representation from neighbors within a finite cutoff, but this locality can miss physical responses that depend on structure beyond the cutoff. Two complementary strategies address this limitation: \emph{nonlocal representation}, which supplies local MLIPs with global structural context, and \emph{nonlocal energy response}, which constructs an explicit nonlocal interaction energy from latent variables such as charges or dipoles. We introduce NoRRA (Nonlocal Representation and Response Augmentation), a plug-in framework that couples both pathways in a local MLIP. Reciprocal-space features inject global periodic context before a replaceable backbone, while a separate nonlocal-response readout predicts constrained latent charges and evaluates an explicit interaction energy through a learnable sum-of-Gaussians kernel. On the same Point Edge Transformer (PET) backbone, NoRRA adds only $0.387\%$ parameters and reduces SPICE relative-energy MAE from the baseline value of $19.798$ to $14.297$~kJ/mol. This framework also transfers to MatterSim. Across molecular, ionic, interfacial, and electrochemical systems, NoRRA improves energy and force accuracy and downstream physical properties, including molten-salt thermal expansion, the liquid structure of NaCl, and the long-range force tails of ion pairs. Component ablations show that the two pathways are complementary, with the largest gains in ionic regimes where Coulomb interactions dominate.

paper.title: Molecular Gating of the Reactive Water Topological Network for Stable Aqueous Zn Batteries
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT The instability of aqueous Zn batteries originates not only from the intrinsic reactivity of water, but also from the continuous hydrogen‐bonded network that enables cooperative interfacial degradation. In conventional aqueous electrolytes, this percolated water network supports proton relay, hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), local alkalization, by‐product precipitation, and Zn 2+ flux distortion, thereby forming a self‐amplifying failure loop at the Zn/electrolyte interface. Herein, we propose a molecular gating strategy to regulate this reactive water network using 4‐hydroxy‐2‐butanone (HBN) as a dual‐site hydrogen‐bond modulator. The carbonyl and hydroxyl groups of HBN competitively interact with water, fragmenting the continuous H 2 O–H 2 O hydrogen‐bond network into low‐cooperativity water domains and suppressing proton‐relay HER. Concurrently, HBN mildly reshapes the Zn 2+ solvation sheath environment toward a less water‐dominated configuration, moderating interfacial charge‑transfer while preserving essential Zn 2+ transport. This topology‐gated aqueous regime simultaneously suppresses water‐induced side reactions, prevents alkaline passivation‐driven Zn 2+ flux distortion, and enables compact Zn deposition. Consequently, the optimized electrolyte affords highly reversible Zn plating/stripping with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.12% over 800 cycles and supports a 1.0 Ah‐level NVO||Zn pouch cell for 70 cycles with negligible capacity decay.

paper.title: ELECTROLYTEMD-BENCH: HOW WELL DO AI AGENTS CONDUCT MOLECULAR DYNAMICS STUDIES ACROSS ELECTROLYTE SOLVATION REGIMES?
paper.abstract: AI agents are advancing the automation of molecular dynamics (MD) research, with the potential to accelerate discovery and design of lithium-battery electrolytes. However, whether they can autonomously complete scientifically reliable electrolyte MD studies remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce ElectrolyteMD-Bench, which unifies dilute, high-concentration, and localized high-concentration electrolytes in a comparative study across distinct solvation regimes. The benchmark connects local coordination, ionic association, single-particle dynamics, and collective transport within one continuous research process. Agents autonomously perform system construction, equilibration, production sampling, property analysis, and cross-system interpretation, while deciding whether to correct errors, continue sampling, or stop. We audit each study along four dimensions: simulation validity, analysis validity, evidence integrity, and outcome calibration. Across eight model–harness configurations, all 24 system runs produced valid production trajectories, yet none of the eight studies satisfied all scientific requirements. Failures included missing analyses, incorrect physical definitions or numerical implementations, insufficient statistical support, and completion claims inconsistent with retained evidence. These results expose a gap between successful MD workflow execution and reliable scientific study completion. ElectrolyteMD-Bench therefore provides a foundational test and defines a key capability threshold that autonomous electrolyte simulation must cross to advance toward computation-first materials exploration.

paper.title: Continuous Single-Droplet Tracking Reveals Scaling Laws of Surface-Confined Mn(II)-Catalyzed SO2 Oxidation
paper.abstract: Abstract Size-dependent kinetics in microdroplets are often used to infer whether reactions occur in the bulk liquid or at the air–water interface, but ensemble measurements can obscure the underlying scaling law. Here, we continuously tracked the radius of one optically levitated droplet to determine reaction location directly from its growth trajectory of the same evolving microdroplet. Benchmark SO2 autoxidation experiments recovered distinct scaling behaviors for bulk reaction at pH 5.0 and interfacial reaction at pH 3.8. Applying the same analysis to Mn(II)-catalyzed SO2 oxidation showed that the catalytically effective Mn inventory is diluted with droplet surface area rather than volume, providing direct dynamic evidence for surface-specific Mn catalysis during sulfate-driven hygroscopic growth. Broadband light-scattering aerosol optical tweezers enabled week-long tracking with nanometer-scale radius precision over a broad size range. The central advance is therefore the continuous one-droplet scaling analysis, which resolves how reaction kinetics evolve together with droplet growth, compositional evolution, and catalyst dilution.

paper.title: Role‐Differentiated Solvation Directs Interfacial Chemistry in Wide‐Temperature Lithium Metal Batteries
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Wide‐temperature lithium metal batteries face intrinsic coupling between bulk transport and interfacial reactivity. Molecules enabling low viscosity and rapid Li + migration can enter the primary solvation sheath and undergo uncontrolled reduction on Li metal. Here, we establish solvation–reactivity decoupling through deliberate molecular role differentiation rather than empirical additive optimization. In the quaternary ester–ether (PADD) electrolyte, methyl propionate (MP) exhibits reduced primary Li + coordination and predominantly promotes fluidity, whereas DME/DOL and FSI − /TFSI − cooperatively reconstruct the reaction‐relevant solvation sheath. Systematic comparison reveals that MP exclusion alone is insufficient; a stable ether–anion network must compensate for the vacated coordination environment. This sheath redirects interfacial reduction toward DOL‐ and anion‐derived products, generating a spatially differentiated PDOL–LiF heteromatrix interphase with a compliant polymer‐rich outer region and a compact LiF‐rich inner framework. The interphase suppresses continuous ester decomposition, lowers nucleation and charge‐transfer barriers, and guides dense Li deposition. Consequently, Li||LiFePO4 cells operate from −30°C to 70°C, retaining 97.1% capacity after 1000 cycles at 25°C and 99.3% after 400 cycles at −30°C. These results identify functional differentiation across bulk electrolyte, solvation sheath, and interphase as a general route to resolve the transport–stability trade‐off in all‐climate lithium metal batteries.

paper.title: Complementary Eigen–Zundel Interpretation Reconciles Thermodynamics and Spectroscopy of Excess Protons in Aqueous HF Solutions
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous solutions of HF and HCl behave very differently at intermediate concentrations: HCl dissociates completely, whereas HFonly partially dissociates and forms bifluoride (). This should lead to markedly different excess‐proton spectra in HF and HCl solutions, in contrast to experimental reports. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, we show that in HF the proton is not firmly bound to , as suggested by textbook chemistry, but dynamically shared with a hydrating water molecule. This is rationalized by a modified Eigen‐picture description which also explains the formation of . The similar vibrational spectra of HF and HCl solutions are explained by a complementary Zundel picture in terms of almost identical excess proton transfer free‐energy profiles for HF and HCl. These results reconcile thermodynamic and spectroscopic observations and provide a unified microscopic picture of excess protons in aqueous solution.

paper.title: Learning from Failure: A Physics-Driven Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Liquid Electrolyte Design
paper.abstract: Liquid electrolytes are foundational to advanced batteries, and their formulation critically affects battery performance, safety, and lifetime. However, designing viable electrolytes remains a longstanding industrial challenge, as it requires navigating an interdependent space of discrete components and continuous concentrations under complex, often conflicting electrochemical constraints. In this work, we introduce SAGE, a Self-improving AGentic framework for Electrolyte discovery that iteratively refines its design policies through physics-driven feedback without human supervision. Central to SAGE is a principled paradigm of self-evolving autonomy, in which the agent iteratively improves through molecular dynamics evaluations and distills case-specific failure experience into actionable guidance for subsequent formulation design. Moreover, SAGE establishes an auditable discovery trajectory that documents constraint violations, retrieved evidence, hypothesis revisions, and resulting policy updates as structured knowledge, providing a reusable blueprint for tackling new scientific problems. Experiments across diverse real-world electrolyte discovery scenarios show the effectiveness of SAGE and the importance of physics-guided self-improvement for designing feasible, novel formulations.

paper.title: Cooperative Relaxation Governs the Viscosity of Ionic Liquids
paper.abstract: Abstract Ionic liquids are promising solvents for batteries, biomass processing and critical mineral recovery, but their viscosities can exceed those of conventional molecular solvents by several orders of magnitude, impeding mass and charge transport and complicating process design. Using complementary neutron spin echo spectroscopy and nuclear magnetic resonance diffusometry, we probe local and long-range dynamics of three protic ionic liquids over time scales from 10–12 to 10–3 seconds. We identify a fast relaxation with closely corresponding self and collective time scales, indicating cooperative rearrangement of the surrounding molecular network. Its characteristic time scale correlates with bulk viscosity, while its temperature dependence reveals distinct Arrhenius activation energies depending on whether extended networks are dominated by hydrogen bonding or electrostatic interactions. These results link cooperative network relaxation to macroscopic viscosity and show how molecular structure can tune the energetic cost of structural relaxation through network connectivity.

paper.title: Ag─S Sites Steer Furfural Electroreduction to Furfuryl Alcohol
paper.abstract: ABSTRACT The electrochemical upgrading of furfural (FF), a biomass‐derived platform molecule, using renewable electricity offers a promising route toward green and sustainable chemical synthesis. However, achieving high selectivity toward hydrogenated products, such as furfuryl alcohol (FA), remains challenging as hydrogenation competes with C─C coupling reactions that generate undesired dimers. In this study, we show that trace sulfide species introduced into the electrolyte dynamically generate Ag─S sites on Ag surfaces during electrolysis, thereby steering the FF reduction reaction toward FA formation. Using Ag disk electrodes, the introduction of 0.5 mM sulfide ions (S 2− ) into the electrolyte increases the Faradaic efficiency (FE) for FA formation from 59% to 88% and enhances its partial current density ( j FA ) from 5.4 to 12.5 mA cm −2 . X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, in situ Raman spectroscopy, and density functional theory simulations collectively reveal that the low‐coverage sulfide species on Ag regulate FF adsorption and facilitate proton transfer to the carbonyl oxygen, steering FA formation, while suppressing hydrofuroin (HF) formation by disrupting the Ag ensembles required for C─C coupling. Overall, our findings establish the deliberate introduction of trace sulfide into the electrolyte as a simple and potentially broadly applicable strategy to steer selectivity in the electrochemical hydrogenation of biomass‐derived furanic aldehydes.

paper.title: Learning Transition-Metal Complexes Reaction Barriers with Active Learning and Machine Learning Interatomic Potential
paper.abstract: Fine-tuning a machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) to accurately model a chemical reaction needs training data along the reaction path. However, that path is exactly what is unknown beforehand. Here we demonstrate a method to efficiently build such a dataset from the only knowledge of the reactant and product. We show that fine-tuning only works when this method is robust. We use a combination of active learning and a custom path generator. This generator is named curved reactive scan, in which each reactive bond follows its own power law, feeding a certified saddle search whose by-products constitute the training set. As a result these data points sit on the reaction path. We show that the fine-tuning is data efficient: for 25 transition-metal complex reactions from the benchmark MOBH35 (15–67 atoms), we generate 86 to 284 density functional theory (ωB97M-V/def2- TZVPD) labels per reaction, and the fine-tuned versions of UMA S 1.2 improve the retrieving of their transition states, forward and reverse energy barriers, at chemical accuracy on average. Those results outperform the pretrained model, even though it was trained on OMol25, a data set that contains reactive configurations generated from these very MOBH35 systems. Our work shows that blind generation of molecular geometries along the reaction path is a crucial step towards efficient MLIP fine-tuning, to potentially unlock applications in metalloprotein studies, and transition metal catalyst discovery.

paper.title: Bonding-Aware Representation Learning for Machine-Learning Force Fields
paper.abstract: Machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) provide a promising framework for modeling molecular energies and forces from atomic configurations. However, most existing MLFFs construct representations from local geometric neighborhoods defined by a fixed cutoff, treating nearby atom pairs primarily through their relative positions. Such representations do not explicitly encode bond connectivity or continuous changes in bond state during dynamics, e.g., reactive dynamics. Consequently, they may struggle to capture the associated variations in energy and force, particularly when the accompanying charge redistribution must satisfy global charge conservation. To address this challenge, we introduce a bond-aware representation framework that models local atom pairs as nodes in a bipartite bond-incidence graph. Each pair is assigned a structured state with orientation-invariant and orientation-equivariant components: the former captures latent bonding information, while the latter encodes signed charge-transfer flow. Aggregation through a signed incidence matrix produces orientation-independent atomic charges while exactly conserving the prescribed total charge. We evaluate our method on rMD17, MD22, Chignolin, Transition1x, and HORM, covering both non-equilibrium and reactive molecular dynamics. Across these benchmarks, our bond-aware model improves energy and force prediction accuracy. Stability analyses and assessments of energy drift further demonstrate the performance of our model in molecular dynamics simulations.

paper.title: Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer Dynamics with Neural Network Potentials and Nuclear Quantum Effects
paper.abstract: Excited-state intramolecular proton transfer is a prototypical ultrafast process that forms the foundation for many chemical and biological phenomena and is highly sensitive to changes in the underlying potential energy landscape. Here, we develop neural network potentials for 10-hydroxybenzo[h]quinoline that describe ground- and excited-state dynamics with near ab initio accuracy. These neural network potentials enable efficient sampling of the proton transfer coordinate and incorporation of nuclear quantum effects through path-integral molecular dynamics. The free energy profiles show that excited-state intramolecular proton transfer proceeds on a largely barrierless excited-state surface, with nuclear quantum effects reducing and smoothing the residual barrier. Non-equilibrium simulations yield an average proton transfer time of ~11.5 fs for quantum hydrogen, consistent with experiment, and reveal a clear isotope effect, with slower dynamics for deuterium and classical nuclei. Mechanistic analysis identifies transient proton donor–acceptor contraction as the key enabling coordinate, while the proton crosses the midpoint prior to reaching the minimum of this coordinate, indicating a dynamically driven transfer. Subtle changes in the conjugated backbone precede proton transfer, reflecting early electronic reorganization and coherent coupling between proton motion and backbone vibrations. Bond-length alternation and vibrational coherence analysis reveal isotope-dependent coherence loss, with deuteration producing stronger damping and more localized proton/backbone dynamics relative to hydrogen. These results establish neural network potential-based approaches as an effective framework for simulating excited-state proton transfer with explicit nuclear quantum effects.
